correctness.rationale: For each zero-containing part, the perfect Italian condition is exactly that the total weight outside the part equals two. The resulting identity R=2q-(q-1)W makes the enumeration exhaustive: q=0 gives all-positive labelings; q=1 forces outside weight two; q at least two permits only total weights two, three, or four, whose support profiles are enumerated disjointly. The packaged checker independently tests the original neighborhood-sum definition on all 748341 ternary labelings across 87 complete multipartite isomorphism types of orders two through nine.

value.rationale: Perfect Italian domination is an established exact-neighbor-weight parameter with published structural, complexity, and algorithmic work. The existing complete-multipartite theorem resolves only the optimum on a restricted part-size domain. The final theorem instead determines the entire feasible labeling space and every weight coefficient for arbitrary part sizes, providing exact counts of minimum and nonminimum configurations and a natural generating-function refinement of the studied optimization problem.
